articles.title: PV Sindhu concerned over financial woes on Europe tour
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu has expressed concern over the financial difficulties faced by Indian shuttlers during their four-tournament
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu has expressed concern over the financial difficulties faced by Indian shuttlers during their four-tournament European campaign, warning that the lack of institutional support could jeopardise the careers of promising youngsters.India’s European swing covered tournaments in Finland, Denmark, France and Germany. With Sports Authority of India (SAI) assistance falling through, several players had to meet expenses out of pocket or seek help from organisations such as Olympic Gold Quest (OGQ). Some younger shuttlers competed without coaches, while others withdrew from tournaments.Reacting on X, Sindhu highlighted the huge disparity between badminton and tennis earnings, pointing out that players in both sports face comparable expenses but vastly different prize money.“A first-round exit at Wimbledon earns £80,000. Winning the China Open, one of badminton’s richest tournaments, earns $140,000. Lose in the first round? Just $2,000,” she wrote on X.Travel, coaching, physiotherapy and other support costs remain substantial in both sports, she said, adding that she had discussed the disparity with former Indian tennis star Rohan Bopanna.Sindhu stressed that not everyone has access to sponsorships and private support. “I’ve been fortunate to have wonderful sponsors, but not everyone has that privilege,” she said. “If I can find ways to fund my tour. But what about the 18-year-old chasing her dreams?” she asked.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka reveals what happened when she teamed up with Tom Brady and David Beckham for an unexpected Holiday project
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka has added an unusual holiday assignment to her busy tennis schedule, joining Tom Brady, David Beckham and Kevin Hart for SharkNinja's
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka has added an unusual holiday assignment to her busy tennis schedule, joining Tom Brady, David Beckham and Kevin Hart for SharkNinja's latest Christmas campaign. The world No. 1 enjoyed the experience more than she expected, particularly because of the company she kept on set. In an interview with Parade, Sabalenka spoke about filming the comedy-filled commercial, her familiarity with SharkNinja products and the role one of its hair tools plays in her routine. She also offered a glimpse into how her family celebrates Christmas.Sabalenka shares her experience working with Tom Brady and David BeckhamThe new campaign, titled "There's No Home Like a SharkNinja Home," brings together four familiar faces for a holiday comedy. Hart plays Beckham's house-sitter while the former England captain enjoys a tropical getaway. Things quickly get out of hand when Hart invites Sabalenka and Brady over.The commercial has no shortage of unusual moments. Hart prepares a turkey using the Ninja Crispi Pro, while Sabalenka helps herself to a frozen drink from the Ninja SLUSHi machine. Brady, meanwhile, wanders around wearing a Shark CryoGlow red light therapy mask and even shakes presents under the Christmas tree.The trouble begins when Hart accidentally breaks a picture frame while vacuuming. Beckham, who has been keeping an eye on his home through a surveillance system, decides to return early. Hart then tries to make things right by offering his unexpected guest a slushie.For Sabalenka, the fun was not limited to what viewers see in the finished advertisement. She said the people involved made the shoot particularly enjoyable."It was so fun," Sabalenka told Parade in an exclusive interview. "The whole campaign is super-fun and when I was told the idea, I was like, ‘Wow that's amazing. I want to jump right in.'"She also enjoyed working alongside Brady and Hart, adding, "Plus these guys, like Kevin and Tom, honestly I was laughing the whole time and the whole idea of the campaign was perfect."The advertisement is the latest chapter in SharkNinja's Neighbors series, which began in 2025 with Beckham and Hart playing next-door neighbors. Earlier instalments featured Beckham's friends enjoying his household products while pretending they were not visiting his home.Aryna Sabalenka explains why SharkNinja products fit her routineThe partnership also made sense outside the commercial. Sabalenka was already using several products from the brand before joining the campaign."I always have a bunch of SharkNinja products at home, including a slushie machine," she explained. "And then, I got introduced to the hair styler, which I love and have been using ever since. I've always had their products, so that's why it was a perfect match."One product she particularly likes is the Shark Glam Hair Styler. Sabalenka said it has become a regular part of getting ready, especially when she wants curls without spending too much time on her hair."I'm no professional but I always do my curls with the SharkNinja and it's great," she said. "It's super-easy to use, even if you're not a pro with styling."She also pointed to hair care as an important reason for using the device. Frequent styling can be a concern, particularly for someone who regularly travels and maintains a demanding athletic routine."It's so good because it's not damaging your hair and that's very important," she explained. "As an athlete, with my hair condition, I'm always trying to use a lot of products for my hair and then, when you have a good hair dryer that's not damaging your hair? It's a game-changer."Sabalenka's Christmas celebrations are much more family-focused than the chaos in the advertisement. She said the occasion usually involves a large dinner, cooking together and dressing up for the gathering."It's always a family dinner and family time," she told Parade. "We cook a lot. We like to look good so we dress up."There is still plenty to manage before everyone sits down to eat. As Sabalenka joked, getting ready while preparing food can be difficult, making the hair styler useful during the rush."But you have to cook for everyone and you don't have much time, so that's why it's a double win because it saves you time," she said.SharkNinja's holiday campaign launched on November 3, bringing Sabalenka into a commercial alongside two of the most recognisable names in global sport.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Winnipeg Jets Snap Nine-Game Losing Streak With Historic NHL-Record Comeback
articles.summary: Trailing by four with minutes remaining, Winnipeg erased a double-digit skid through a record-breaking scoring frenzy before Dylan Samberg’s overtime heroics...
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets didn't just snap their nine-game losing streak on Tuesday night. They made NHL history in the process.

Trailing 4-0 with just 2:39 remaining in regulation, Winnipeg mounted a remarkable comeback, scoring four goals in a franchise-record two minutes and six seconds before Dylan Samberg completed the stunning turnaround with his first goal of the season in overtime.

The comeback established an NHL record for the latest a team has overcome a four-goal deficit, turning what appeared to be a certain 10th consecutive loss into one of the most improbable finishes in league history.

Kyle Connor scored twice in the final minute of the third period, recording his 12th and 13th goals of the season as the Jets somehow erased a four-goal deficit in the dying moments of regulation.

The historic finish came during an eventful third period that also saw captain Adam Lowry drop the gloves and rookie defenceman Tyrel Bauer complete a Gordie Howe hat trick, registering a goal, an assist and a fight in the final frame.

Somehow, Stuart Skinner emerged with the victory in goal, despite the Jets trailing by four goals with less than three minutes remaining.

The improbable victory also provided a much-needed reprieve for head coach Scott Arniel, whose team appeared destined for a 10th consecutive defeat before its stunning late-game heroics.

For a Winnipeg team desperately searching for a way to end its nine-game skid, Tuesday's victory delivered just a bit more than two points in the standings. It was probably a season-saver.

articles.title: Kochetkov suffers first loss as Predators down Hurricanes 4-1
articles.summary: As tends to happen when the opponent is Nashville, the Canes got Saros’d
articles.body:
Eventually the Hurricanes were going to lose again.

One of the biggest truisms in the NHL is that good goaltending will beat just about anyone, especially on any given night. For the Hurricanes, Juuse Saros is on the list of players who just manage to elevate to a different level when they are across the ice. It happened again Tuesday Night as he made 29 saves in a 4-1 Nashville win over Carolina.

On the other side, Pyotr Kochetkov did what he could to keep Carolina into the game, but his 16 saves were not enough as frustration mounted and despite dominating the first period Carolina went into the locker room down 1-0.

Nick Perbix was the one who got the party started in Music City late in the first, as Nashville had one of their few sustained pressure sessions of the period. They didn't waste it as Filip Forsberg was able to jar the puck away from Sean Walker, and feed a perfect pass over to Perbix for the shot. Perbix used the traffic in front of the net to blast it by Kochetkov, and while Rod Brind'Amour called his timeout to try and see if the play were either offside or there should have been a high stick stoppage, he ultimately let it go.

Forsberg would figure into the second goal in the next period, this time on a rush Nashville was able to get it deep and Forsberg would keep the puck from going out at the blue line. He feathered a great pass over to an open Roman Josi to give Nashville a 2-0 lead.

Carolina would claw one back a few minutes later, though, as the white-hot Jackson Blake wouldn't be denied. Blake would pass ahead over to a rushing Shayne Gostisbehere, and as he went in on Saros he passed it back to Blake who took one shot and then immediately roofed the rebound to claw Carolina back to 2-1.

That unfortunately would be the high point of the night for Carolina as while they would win the third period on shots 12-8, they couldn't generate much of anything offensively. Kochetkov made several huge stops in the period to keep it close, but about five minutes in, he was unable to stop a great deflection by Adam Edstrom. Josi would peel back to the blue line and put on a shot that was about crest-level to Edstrom. Edstrom took his stick and deflected it back down to where Kochetkov couldn't recover. The league checked the height of the stick and Brind'Amour wouldn't challenge the call.

Carolina would get a few chances with the empty net, but ultimately Ross Colton would get in all alone—with Brady Skjei and Jack Drury each getting a point versus their old teammates for good measure.

The loss drops Carolina to 12-3-2 on the season, and Kochetkov to 10-1.

Carolina is heading up to Long Island next, practicing at the Islanders' facility on Wednesday before facing off against the Isles Thursday. That will be an ESPN+/Hulu exclusive game—and it will also be the first time Carolina faces a team that plays in their Hometown Remix Sweaters. Carolina will then host Chicago in a later faceoff Saturday before they fly out to Finland.

articles.title: Wright accounts for 4TDs to send Buffalo past Miami (Ohio) 34-31 in OT
articles.summary: MIAMI, Ohio (AP) — Jason Wright threw for 358 yards and accounted for four touchdowns and Buffalo rallied in the fourth quarter to beat Miami of Ohio 34-31 i...
articles.body:
MIAMI, Ohio (AP) — Jason Wright threw for 358 yards and accounted for four touchdowns and Buffalo rallied in the fourth quarter to beat Miami of Ohio 34-31 in overtime on Tuesday night.

Wright threw for two touchdowns and ran for two scores. Chance Morrow had 199 yards on 12 receptions and two touchdowns for Buffalo.

Caleb Heavener threw for 154 yards and a touchdown, and a D'Shawntae Jones ran for 117 yards on 12 carries for Miami.

After Oliver Hautanen made a 27-yard field goal to give the Bulls (6-3, 4-1 Mid-American) a 34-31 lead in its half of the first overtime, Miami's Kellan McLaughlin missed a 45-yard field goal attempt to end the game.

Wright's 2-yard touchdown run with 1:35 left in regulation ended a 12-play, 80-yard drive that brought Buffalo into a 31-all tie.

Almost 7 1/2 minutes prior, Wright threw a 4-yard scoring pass to Chance Morrow to end an 11-play, 75-yard drive to get the Bulls within 31-24.

Scoop Smith's 6-yard touchdown run with 12:01 remaining gave Miami (5-4, 3-2) its largest lead at 31-16.

Buffalo: Travels to face Ball State on Nov. 11.

articles.title: Timberwolves’ Norchad Omier changes mind on two-way contract, joins Cavs instead
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves will have to look elsewhere in their bid to fill their open two-way roster spot after Norchad Omier reneged on his agreement with...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves will have to look elsewhere in their bid to fill their open two-way roster spot after Norchad Omier reneged on his agreement with the Timberwolves to sign a two-way contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers instead. Michael Scotto of HoopsHype was the first to report this development .

Omier was with the Los Angeles Clippers last season and suited up in six games, averaging 2.8 minutes in 4.0 minutes of play. The 6-foot-5 power forward spent the vast majority of last season in the G League, splitting time with the Cleveland Charge, the Cavs' affiliate, and San Diego Clippers, the Clippers' affiliate.

Perhaps Omier decided to sign with the Cavs instead since he's more familiar with the team, having suited up in a total of 31 G-League games for the Charge. But Omier did suit up for the Timberwolves in preseason, playing in all six games for the team and averaging 1.8 points in 8.0 minutes per contest.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Backing out of an agreement with an NBA team is almost unprecedented, but turnabout's fair play. In recent days, the Oklahoma City Thunder backed out of a reported agreement with free agent Ochai Agbaji, with the Thunder reportedly wanting to reassess their roster in light of Chet Holmgren's recent injury that will keep him out for months.

The Thunder have since signed Dalen Terry to a two-year contract to fill their open roster spot.

The Timberwolves recently waived Enrique Freeman after he suffered an injury that would keep him out for weeks, opening up a two-way roster spot in the process. Freeman is a 6-foot-9 power forward, while Omier is also listed as a four, so it makes sense that the Timberwolves will be looking for another power forward on the market.

They currently have Rocco Zikarsky and Zyon Pullin as their two other two-way players on the roster.

Considering that the Timberwolves will be without Anthony Edwards for up to two months after he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, Minnesota will need warm bodies they can rely on in case other injury problems open up playing time for those who are buried in the depth chart.

articles.title: Ziaire Williams gets candid on ‘easy’ role alongside Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers’ current win streak hit two games following their 138-117 thrashing of the Miami Heat on Monday, and the team welcomed t...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers ' current win streak hit two games following their 138-117 thrashing of the Miami Heat on Monday, and the team welcomed the return of forward Ziaire Williams. The six-year veteran had been sidelined for three games due to a foot injury , but he was cleared to go, picking up right where he left off prior to sitting out.

Although Ziaire Williams had been in the starting lineup to begin the season, he came off the Lakers' bench in the win against the Heat, contributing nine points on 3-of-6 shooting from the 3-point line. Williams has been one of the team's most dependable 3&D players , along with Matisse Thybulle, and for him, the uptick in his shooting efficiency is due to the players he's playing alongside.

"They're easy looks, way easier than they've been in the past. Like I said, they're sending two to Luka [Doncic], two to AR [Austin Reaves] every time," Williams said during his postgame press conference after the win against the Heat. "It's just swing, swing, one more and I get to set my feet, get to square up the ball. I put a lot of work this summer. [I'm] trusting my work, confident in my shot, my shot feels great. I put the reps in, so I just got to trust it."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Through five games this season, Williams is shooting career-highs across the board. He's up to 55.9 percent from the field and 46.7 percent from the 3-point line. His previous career-bests in shooting efficiency was 45 percent from the field and 34.3 percent from 3-point range. He's right at his career averages in shot attempts as well with 6.8 overall field goal attempts and 4.2 3-point attempts.

And he's averaging a career-high in points with 10.8. Prior to his return from injury, his points per game average was 11.3. Williams' production is key to the Lakers' success, especially when it comes to playing off Doncic. Teams have begun to trap and blitz Doncic, and the Lakers haven't done so well in responding to that type of defense in the early-goings of the season.

But against the Heat, the team did a much better job at reacting and adjusting to the defense. While it's still a work in progress, Williams believes the team has the right mentality and personnel to continue countering what opposing teams through at them defensively.

"[It's] a lot of good reps of practicing. They send two on the ball, there's always going to be a 4-on-3 advantage on the back side. It's just about countering on those advantages, looking opposite for corner threes, finishing at the rim," Williams said. "The short roll is so important with those blitzes cause it opens up the floor for all of us. And that's the beauty of our team. You can put different guys at different spots and everyone is able to make plays. …

"All our guys are just dynamic and versatile and everyone just wants to make the right play. No one wants to only shoot. There's no egos and that's the fun part about it. We all want to see each other succeed and we have that mindset that good things are gonna happen."

articles.title: Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request
articles.summary: Nikita Kucherov wants out of the Tampa Bay Lightning, but he still can’t stop going all out for his team. Reports surfaced last Friday that the 33-year-old...
articles.body:
Nikita Kucherov wants out of the Tampa Bay Lightning , but he still can't stop going all out for his team.

Reports surfaced last Friday that the 33-year-old Kucherov had already asked the Lightning to move him. In the two games since, the two-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner has done nothing on the ice but rack up points.

Against the Nashville Predators on Saturday on the road, Kucherov had a hand in three of his team's goals, as he recorded a trio of assists, albeit in a 5-4 shootout loss to Steven Stamkos and company.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Bolts returned to action on Tuesday, and Kucherov was clearly still feeling it, adding two more assists to his total in the 2026-27 NHL season. This time around, his effort did not go for naught, with the Lightning defeating the Detroit Red Wings, 4-2.

Kucherov is in a contract year, which means he is on track to become a free agent next summer. However, he also clarified that his trade request is less about money and more about the perceived disrespect he feels from Tampa Bay over its "poor communication."

It remains to be seen how this saga between Kucherov and the Lightning will conclude, but what seems to be clear is that he is not shortchanging the only team he's played for so far in his NHL career when it comes to his effort and production on the ice.

Kucherov and the Lightning improved to 9-3-2 after the win against Detroit. Up next for them is a date with the visiting Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday.

articles.title: Viola Station 107: The more things change
articles.summary: Mike, Mike, and Tito recorded this pre-Sassuolo and now realize that maybe we were a tad bit down.
articles.body:
So full disclosure: we recorded this before the Sassuolo game . And our collective emotional state was considerably lower. We were, in fact, struggling with our feelings. The podcast reflects that because, in hindsight, we were a little bit grim about Fiorentina's prospects going forward. That's apparent in pretty much everything we discussed.

What did we discuss? Well, we ran through the recent history, picking our standouts (big dogs, boneheads, et cetera) before considering some tactical and statistical stuff which, in hindsight, probably doesn't matter as much after Fiorentina got its wait a minute second? That can't be right, can it? Second win of the season? Okay, yeah, maybe we weren't entirely wrong in being ruffled. That Relegation Percent-O-Meter still resembles the Doomsday Clock.

On the plus side, we got a wonderful McMike milestone, some unexpectedly terse Producer Mike analysis, and Tito completely failing to throw to an advertisement correctly. articles.title: Emiliano Martínez, Valentín Barco, Aarón Anselmino called up by Argentina
articles.summary: Some surprising selections from Argentina
articles.body:
There's an international break after this weekend's matches, but for a fair few Chelsea boys, there will be no rest. And among those set for national team duty are our trio or Argentinians.

Trio? — you might ask. Who all could that be? After all, Enzo Fernández is gone. Alejandro Garnacho is gone. And Emi Martínez has a broken face. Who's left? Valentín Barco. Sure. Get in the chopper!

But joining Barco are indeed Martínez, and, in an even bigger surprise, Aarón Anselmino — man with no actual minutes of competitive senior football yet this season. Maybe Argentina just want their own Estêvão situation.

Argentina are playing only a couple friendlies during this break, against Uruguay and Costa Rica, and manager Lionel Scaloni is using this opportunity to check out some fresh faces. Anselmino is one of two players called up with zero senior caps, and one of nine with less than five. (Barco himself is barely above that threshold at seven.)

And Emi's inclusion is hopefully a good sign that is recovery from the fractured jaw he suffered against Everton a few weeks ago is going well. Let's see that mask!

articles.title: Bulls Reportedly Open to Trading All-Star as Deadline Approaches
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls could have a decision to make involving one of their offseason additions. According to NBA insider Jake Fischer, Chicago is looking to fiel...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls could have a decision to make involving one of their offseason additions. According to NBA insider Jake Fischer, Chicago is looking to field offers for Norman Powell ahead of the trade deadline. The report puts a scorer into a conversation about how the Bulls intend to build their future.

For fans, the development raises a question beyond whether Powell can help another team. Chicago added him to strengthen its offense and provide experience around younger players. Listening to offers would require weighing those benefits against whatever another organization might offer.

Jake Fischer Reports Bulls' Interest in Norman Powell Offers

Fischer's reported update concerns Chicago's willingness to consider offers. It does not establish that a trade has been agreed upon or identify a confirmed destination.

That distinction matters because availability alone does not determine a player's return. Other teams must evaluate fit, salary and the assets they would need to surrender. Chicago would then have to decide whether the package improves its position enough to justify losing Powell.

Powell joined the Bulls after earning his first All-Star selection with Miami last season. His agreement includes a team option for the second season, giving Chicago a future decision beyond the trade market. That structure leaves the organization multiple paths to consider.

The basketball appeal for a potential buyer is straightforward. Additional perimeter scoring can help a team when its primary options face extra defensive attention. Powell's experience could make him attractive to an organization seeking immediate offensive support rather than another developmental project.

What a Powell Trade Could Mean for Chicago

For the Bulls, however, moving a veteran should involve more than making room. Younger players benefit from opportunities, but they also need functional lineups and experienced teammates. Chicago must assess whether a deal supplies value without making development harder elsewhere.

Keeping Powell carries its own argument. A reliable scoring presence can reduce the pressure on less experienced players and help an offense survive difficult stretches. Those contributions deserve consideration alongside draft picks or younger players that might appear in hypothetical offers.

The decision ultimately comes down to what becomes available. A strong proposal could give Chicago a reason to adjust its plans. A disappointing market could make retaining Powell the more sensible choice.

Fischer's report makes Powell a name to monitor, not a player already departing. Bulls fans should watch the offers and reporting before judging the outcome.

articles.title: Kentucky Gets Major Boost From Iowa State Transfer in Season Debut
articles.summary: Kentucky forward Milan Momcilovic impressed in his first game as a Wildcat. Momcilovic scored a game-high 24 points in Kentucky’s 85-57 win over Manhattan. T...
articles.body:
Kentucky forward Milan Momcilovic impressed in his first game as a Wildcat. Momcilovic scored a game-high 24 points in Kentucky's 85-57 win over Manhattan. The Iowa State transfer knocked down six of his nine three-point attempts.

Momcilovic made eight of his 12 shot attempts from the field and shot 66.7% from three. This allowed him to get a very efficient 24 points in 28 minutes of playing time. He looked very confident out there and worked perfectly for this Wildcat offense.

Momcilovic didn't get his first points until 7:21 left in the first half, when he knocked down a three. After he made that three, he was on fire, letting the game come to him. All it took for him to get going was to see the ball go through once, and he started hitting everything.

At Iowa State, Momcilovic averaged 16.9 points and shot 48.7% from three, which is unbelievably good. That alone made him a big target for Kentucky to go out and try to get him. A good three-point shooter is what the Wildcats have needed, but instead they got a great three-point shooter.

Momcilovic also earned second-team All-Big 12 honors. Kentucky brought him in so he could provide elite three-point shooting, and in one game, it looks like it's already paying off. He did what the Wildcats' offense needed him to do and is a player to watch out for going forward.

Momcilovic can stretch the defense out and force teams to guard him close. This allows players to penetrate and have a layup, or if the defense helps off of Momcilovic, he will be wide open for a three. He makes teams have to guard differently and causes pressure and rotational problems.

He showed out in his first game as a Wildcat; he provided the lethal shooting that he is known for. This is a good sign for a team that needed more shooting last season. He will be important to everything that Kentucky wants to do this whole season; he may be their most valuable piece.

articles.title: Jets beat Canadiens in OT after trailing 4-0 with 3 minutes left, setting NHL record
articles.summary: The Jets won a game in a way never before seen in the NHL on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets snapped a nine-game winless streak with one of the most unlikely wins in NHL history on Tuesday.

With less than three minutes remaining in a game against the Montreal Canadiens, the Jets trailed 4-0. The game ended as a 5-4 win in overtime, with Dylan Samberg scoring the game-winning goal. Per ESPN , it's the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history.

That record was previously held by the 2007-08 Los Angeles Kings, who began their comeback with 7:14 remaining.

Tyrel Bauer the Jets' first goal with 2:38 left in the third period. Morgan Barron added another with 1:57 left. Kyle Connor made it a one-goal game with 1:00 left. Then an Alexandre Carrier tripping penalty gave Winnipeg a power play, which Connor converted with 33 seconds left to send the game to overtime.

There's sugarcoating that for the Canadiens. This is a Jets team that entered the game with a 4-8-3 record. This is a Jets team was on a nine-game winless streak. This a Jets team that lost its previous game 7-0, to the Carolina Hurricanes on Sunday. This is a Jets team that traded its Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender away not even two weeks ago .

Montreal not only choked away a four-point lead, they allowed the Jets' quickest four-goal sequence since 1984, per ESPN. Canadiens star Cole Caufield summed things up after the game, via the Montreal Gazette :

"Some of us thought the game was over," Caufield said. "We had a four-goal lead. There's no excuse for this. It's terrible."

Embarrassments abound, though it's perhaps worth noting the Canadiens have been without captain Nick Suzuki for six straight games due to a hand injury.

articles.title: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals
articles.summary: Mackinaw City and Burt Lake Northern Michigan Christian Academy rolled to MHSAA district volleyball semifinal victories on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
MACKINAW CITY — Mackinaw City will play for an MHSAA Division 4 district volleyball title .

Taking on Mackinac Island in a district semifinal , the Comets booked their ticket to a championship clash at St. Ignace by capturing a 3-0 victory (25-12, 25-11, 25-16) over the Lakers in Mackinaw City on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

After starting slow and trailing 7-1 in the first set, the Comets (13-22-5) regrouped, battled back and took a one-set lead in the match. From there, they were in cruise control behind quality offensive and defensive play.

"Once we were able to get ourselves settled, we played some very solid volleyball tonight and did a great job of getting into our system offensively, and our defense did a great job of digging balls and keeping balls alive to give ourselves a shot at winning some long volleys," Mackinaw City coach Jake Huffman said.

Rian Esper's 10 kills, six aces and six digs fueled the Comets, who received 16 assists, seven digs, two kills and seven digs from Julia Short, and 11 digs, six assists, four kills and three aces from Emily Kruczynski. Mackinaw City's many other contributors included Alaia Mendez (eight kills, five aces, four digs), Poppy Wallace (five kills, two digs, one block), Ella Kruczynski (six aces, five digs, one assist), and Sarah Lentell (two kills, one dig).

"I was very happy with our response and proud of the effort that ladies put forth tonight," Huffman said. "We will use (Wednesday) to prep for a very tough St. Ignace squad on Thursday."

Thursday's district final at St. Ignace (10-11-7) is a 6 p.m. start.

Eagles beat Alanson, will meet Harbor Light for title

HARBOR SPRINGS — Get ready for a Northern Lakes Conference showdown for the district title on Thursday.

Opening its postseason in style was the Burt Lake Northern Michigan Christian Academy volleyball team, which earned a 3-0 victory over Alanson (25-17, 25-10, 25-15) in an MHSAA Division 4 semifinal at Harbor Light on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

The Eagles (23-6-2) were led by Shanna Ferraiuolo, who finished with 21 kills and four digs, while Lauren Ferraiuolo tallied 18 kills, three aces and three digs, and Hazel Bowman added 38 assists and three aces. Isabel Hoffmeyer chipped in with 12 digs.

"Always nice to get a postseason win," NMCA coach Josh Ferraiuolo said. "We were a little rusty after being off for more than a week, but overall, we played pretty well. Looking forward to a very competitive final on Thursday."

NMCA faces Harbor Light (16-6-6) in a 6 p.m. final on Thursday, Nov. 5, at Harbor Light. Harbor Light defeated Pellston 3-0 (25-14, 25-16, 25-7) in a semifinal on Tuesday.

Inland Lakes falls to Harbor Springs in 3

CHARLEVOIX — The Inland Lakes volleyball team's season ended following a 3-0 loss to Harbor Springs (22-25, 23-25, 24-26) in an MHSAA Division 3 district first-round match in Charlevoix on Monday, Nov. 2.

"The girls battled hard all night, we had great contributions from every player on the team. Unfortunately, we just struggled putting the ball away in those high-pressure situations, and Harbor capitalized on that," Inland Lakes coach Shaylee Michael said.

Ava Belford finished with 11 kills, six digs and one ace to lead the Bulldogs (10-21-4), while Adisyn Fenstermaker tallied 11 digs, three kills and two aces, Mariah King had 22 assists, 10 digs, four kills and one ace, Emmalynn Connelly added seven kills, one ace and one block, and Khali Woollard collected 12 digs and one ace.

"This team has made immense progress from the beginning of the season to now, and I am very proud of the work they have put in," Michael said.

articles.title: OTD (4/11/1972): Billy Elliott’s Sunderland Debut Brings Fireworks
articles.summary: Billy Elliott took temporary charge after Alan Brown's shock departure in November 1972. Could his first game at the helm spark a revival at Roker Park?
articles.body:
Alan Brown was not the first manager I experienced at Roker Park, but he was the manager I grew up with. His departure was something of a shock to me as a young fan. I had assumed that, like my parents, he would always be there!

Billy Elliott had been shown the door at Roker Park as a player by Alan Brown in 1957. He had then been invited back as a coach in 1968. One of Elliott's first jobs was coaching the youth team and, in 1969, he coached that team to the FA Youth Cup final and victory.

Fourteen games into the 1972/73 season, with the club in 14th position in the table and gates dipping below 12,000, Brown resigned and Billy Elliott was installed as caretaker manager whilst the board figured out if they could get Clough or Revie (the fans' choice) in as Brown's replacement.

Aston Villa at Roker Park was to be Elliott's first game in temporary control.

Typical of the blunt-speaking Yorkshireman that he was, he told Ken Gorman of The Journal: "I am no stuffed dummy, I wouldn't worry about having to speak my mind to anyone, including our directors."

Elliott was 47 years old at the time. He had gained five England caps as a player at Bradford, Burnley and Sunderland, before finishing off at non-league Wisbech Town, having been released by Brown.

Hanging up his boots, Elliott had gone on to coach the Libyan national team, USA servicemen in Germany and manage Belgian club Royal Daring, before coming back to Roker Park as part of Brown's coaching team.

For his first game in temporary control, he wasted no time in making some tough decisions. He dropped Joe Bolton and John Lathan and relegated Mick McGiven to the subs' bench, bringing in transfer-listed Keith Coleman and Brian Chambers, as well as Billy Hughes, who had just come off the transfer list.

He moved Bobby Kerr back to the right-hand side of midfield and opted for a very attacking line-up to try and end a run of one point from four games.

Aston Villa, like Sunderland, were something of a sleeping giant. Managed by the experienced Vic Crowe, they were pushing hard for promotion and were well in touch at this point in the season. Even though the dangerous forward Andy Lochhead was not available, Villa had a strong squad that included some players who would go on to have fine careers. The likes of Chris Nicholl, John Gidman, Alun Evans, Brian Little and Bruce Rioch were players who would grace the game for a generation.

Sunderland's biggest gate of the season, 7,000 up on the last home game, turned up to see if the team could react to Alan Brown's departure – and what a spirited, all-action performance they saw.

I had just made it to my left-of-centre position in the Fulwell End when Villa captain Bruce Rioch attempted a long diagonal pass back to his keeper. The ball fell invitingly for the returning Billy Hughes, who strode majestically forward, rounded Cumbes in the Villa goal and nonchalantly put the ball in the back of the net. What a start to the game and what a roar it got from the crowd.

Hughesie had a characteristic way of marking his goals, and I can picture him still, arms aloft, strutting like a peacock and milking the applause. He knew how to celebrate a goal and work the crowd, did Billy!

The goal was the signal for Sunderland to pour forward at every opportunity, and for 20 minutes Villa could hardly get a touch as Ian Porterfield stroked the ball all over the park to ready and willing team-mates eager to add to the lead they had taken. Cumbes more than earned his match bonus in this period alone, as he just about kept Villa in the game.

It was typical of the way things had gone for us in this season so far that the first error made led to a Villa equaliser.

Keith Coleman had enjoyed a great opening period to the game, with a couple of good runs, solid tackles and interventions, as well as some clever use of the ball. Despite being a big Joe Bolton fan, I always thought Coleman worked in well with Ian Porterfield on that left-hand side.

One area of his game that needed work, in my opinion (as a young teenage expert!), was his tendency towards an impetuous challenge. He went for a tackle he had no right to go for against Bruce Rioch, who slipped the challenge and, in the space he had created, slammed a cracking shot from the edge of the box that went in off the foot of the post. It was a good goal by Rioch, who probably felt he needed to atone for his opening-minute error.

Rioch then took the game by the scruff of its neck and had two blockbuster attempts that caused a bit of frantic defending. His first shot had Jimmy Montgomery scuttling across his goal as the ball flew just past the post. Then another shot, which was goalbound, cannoned off a defender and fell to Evans in the box. His attempt was cleared brilliantly off the line by Dick Malone.

Back came Sunderland through Dennis Tueart. A drive down the right wing led to a powerful shot that Cumbes saved, diving full-length. Moments later, Tueart came down the left wing and cannoned a shot that had the Fulwell End surging in anticipation of the net rippling. The ball sped just past the post.

Half-time saw the Lads warmly applauded from the pitch. It had been a pulsating 45 minutes.

The second half resumed in the same fashion as the first, with both teams looking for the next goal. It was a sharp contrast to some of the games in the latter days of Alan Brown's reign, where low-risk, careful football appeared to be what the Sunderland team had been instructed to deliver.

Evans beat Richie Pitt all ends up with a mazy run and short pass to Peterlee-born Brian Little, whose attempt produced a marvellous point-blank save from Monty.

Rioch was influencing the game in every way possible, as he brought down Tueart right on the byline just after the hour. Ian Porterfield stepped up to take the kick and, with a clever feint, caressed a ball into the near post when it looked like he was going longer. The ball looked, in that split-second, as if it was going to nobody in particular, when a galloping Bobby Kerr arrived and got an angled touch with his head that deflected the ball at pace, across the keeper and in at the far post. If that was a rehearsed move, it was a cracker. The ground erupted as Bobby blessed us with his trademark forward-roll celebration.

Villa were no soft touch at this time and came back strongly. Just six minutes after conceding, they were back level. I remember this as a bit of a soft goal. An aimless cross looped into the box that should have been dealt with (highlighting a difficulty in the air defensively). Brian Little, possibly the second smallest player on the pitch behind Bobby Kerr, rose to get a scruffy touch on the ball. Montgomery might have done better with this one, but it seemed as if the awkward contact created a moment of indecision and the ball looped limply over his head and crept into the net at the angle of the bar and post.

It was a bit of a sickener, but back came Sunderland, with Porterfield finding a great pass to Watson (who had been engaged in a cracking contest with Villa centre-half Chris Nicholl for most of the game). His attempt was only an inch or two past the post.

What then ensued was a ding-dong battle as both teams went for the winner. Sunderland probably came the closest to finding this in the very last minute of the game, when Tueart had another rousing run and rasping shot that was saved by Cumbes at his near post.

On reflection, a draw was probably a fair result. Porterfield was player of the match for me, but honourable mentions go to Tueart and Kerr. The three lads returning to the team gave Elliott something to ponder for the next game, with Chambers showing some nice touches in midfield.

Villa manager Vic Crowe was satisfied with the result that kept his team in the promotion race. He told reporters: "It was a hard match played at a terrific pace."

Billy Elliott was delighted with the effort from his team, so much so that he gave them an extra day off.

The point gained actually saw Sunderland drop a place to 15th in the table, which seemed scant reward for the effort and application delivered.

Elliott hinted to The Journal's Ken Gorman that his relatively inexperienced defence was his priority and that he was considering moving Dave Watson back to centre-half, but would talk this through with Watson. Richie Pitt and Mickey Horswill had been given a torrid afternoon by Evans and Little, but had nonetheless stuck at their task.

Reflecting back on this moment, Dave Watson said: "Billy Elliott always thought I was wasted at centre-forward and that I had much more to give the team at centre-half. I had done alright as a centre-half playing centre-forward, but I felt much happier playing number five. I think Billy saw that and he thought I should be playing at the back, so he moved me there at the earliest opportunity."

Watson was moved back for the next game at Carlisle and, for all bar three games, he played in the number five shirt for the rest of the season, going on to have a stellar career at club and international level as a centre-half.

Elliott's (first) caretaker spell would only last for four games, as Bob Stokoe came in from left field to take the manager's post.

I do not think many of us could have envisaged, at this stage of the season, that we would finish a credible sixth in the table and that we would be FA Cup winners by the end of the campaign. A reminder of how quickly things can turn around in football.

Division Two Date – 04.11.1972 Venue – Roker Park Attendance – 18,717 Sunderland 2 – 2 Aston Villa Goal-scorers – Hughes 1 min; Rioch 20 min; Kerr 62 min; Little 67 min. Sunderland – Montgomery; Malone; Coleman; Horswill; Pitt; Kerr; Chambers; Porterfield; Hughes; Watson; Tueart. Sub – McGiven. Aston Villa – Cumbes; Gidman; Aitken; Nicholl; Turnbull; Ross; Rioch; Vowden; Anderson; Little; Evans. Sub – Brown.

articles.title: Fan Letters: ‘We Need To Get Behind The Manager And The Lads’
articles.summary: Letters of support for Regis Le Bris!
articles.body:
We need to get behind the manager and the Lads. We've seen what constant change looks like, and it hasn't exactly been a roaring success. New managers, new philosophies, rebuilding the squad every 12 months. At some point, you have to trust the process and give people time to develop. We've spent years demanding a long-term plan, but some supporters seem unwilling to tolerate the patience required to make one work.

Getting Brobbey and Ballard back are big steps in the right direction. Injuries and a harsh hand from the fixture computer have contributed to the position we sit in the table. Yes, the players and the manager could also do better, but something positive is just around the corner.

Let's not end up like the shower up the road, who boo their team off the park at half-time and full-time. We're better than that.

Editor's note [Martin] Thanks for the email Steve. We've all seen what happens when we don't have stability – no one wants to go back to those days. Similarly, I'm sure the vast majority of us want Regis Le Bris to enjoy more and more success here. Change doesn't automatically mean things are going to go well – nor does it mean they're going to go badly. Le Bris staying doesn't guarantee either of those either. We can all see where we need to improve, and the reality is the players' performance hasn't been good enough this season, and neither have results. The ideal is Le Bris is able to change that – the question is how long can the club wait for things to change? I believe the playing squad is more than capable of competing towards the top third of the league, and I suspect the club believe that too. So putting sentiment and the past to one side, he needs to start getting results over the next couple of months, or he'll be replaced.

I think Sunderland supporters should give credit where it's due for what Régis has done over the three years he's been with us.

After all, look how long it took Sir Alex Ferguson to get there when he was manager. So come on, supporters, give Régis a chance. He's the best manager we've had in years.

Editor's note [Martin] Thanks for the email Ian. I don't think anyone would fail to give Le Bris credit for what he's achieved in the 2 seasons he's had here. Hopefully he'll turn this situation around – however if a new manager had come in in the summer and the team was producing this level of performance and results he'd likely already have gone. Football moves quickly, it's a results business, you know the cliches, and if things don't drastically pick up soon we'll be in massive trouble. The Ferguson example is relevant, albeit in a different era. But I bet there aren't many Man Utd fans who in hindsight say ''we should have kept big Ron". Sometime change is necessary. I'm hoping Le Bris turns this round, I genuinely am, but he needs results, quickly.

articles.title: Manchester City may have only scratched the surface of Elliot Anderson’s enormous potential
articles.summary: Elliot Anderson has made a strong start to his Manchester City career. The England international has firmly established himself as a key component of Manches...
articles.body:
Elliot Anderson has made a strong start to his Manchester City career. The England international has firmly established himself as a key component of Manchester City's midfield. His tireless work rate, ability to win duels and quality in possession make Anderson the fulcrum of City's midfield. However, as impressive as Anderson has been there is a scary thought for Manchester City's rivals to consider. Anderson has barely scratched the surface of the midfielder he could become. That is an exciting prospect to consider as Enzo Maresca raised this possibility yesterday.

Enzo Maresca believes that Elliot Anderson has the ability to play in a more advanced midfield role.

Manchester City manager has used Elliot Anderson primarily as a number six in midfield this season. The endless energy that Anderson has makes him a quality number six. Couple this with his quality in possession and his strengths in duels, Anderson is the player for City to build their midfield around. Speaking yesterday, ahead of Manchester City's Champions League league phase fixture against RB Leipzig, Enzo Maresca explained that Anderson has the ability to play as a number eight in midfield. Maresca believes that Anderson has the ability to arrive in the box and add more goals to his game. He explained: " I think in this moment he is playing in the position which is best for him. That is a holding midfielder like a six. "

" No doubt in the future he can be also a number eight and arrive in the box. He has a good pass and also I think he can score some more goals ."

" In this moment I'm trying to know all of them in the right way. It's just been four months so I need to know them better and they need to know me better. It's on both sides. But for sure he can be a number eight that arrives inside the box."

Once Elliot Anderson adds more goals and assists to his game he will be the complete midfield weapon for Manchester City.

It hasn't taken long at all for Elliot Anderson to show why Manchester City were so eager to sign him from Nottingham Forest. Anderson has been Manchester City's standout player alongside Erling Haaland for the 2026-27 season. The fact that the 23-year-old midfielder has cast aside any pressure of the heavy price that City paid to sign him is a credit to him. As Anderson is only 23, it does bode well for how much more he can grow as a player.

Elliot Anderson has the potential to add goals and assists to his game. At times, Anderson moves like De Bruyne. Anderson will never be the type of midfielder that De Bruyne was. No player ever will be. However, Anderson's passing game shares traits with De Bruyne. In time, it will not be a surprise to see Anderson become a regular provider of assists for Manchester City.

Also, Anderson has the potential to score goals from midfield. As he develops, or plays alongside Ayyoub Bouaddi more often, there is no reason why Anderson can't follow in Rodri's footsteps and add goals while playing as a number six.

As good as Elliot Anderson already is as a player, he has scratched the surface of what he will become. Manchester City already have a monster in midfield in Anderson. Once he develops and adds goals and assists on a consistent basis to his play, he will be a nightmare for Manchester City's opponents to contend with.
